ch35.title: Peter's Confession
ch35.b002: Before he took the twelve north to Caesarea-Philippi, Jesus wanted to see his family once more. David Zebedee, working with Jude, Jesus’ brother, arranged for the whole Nazareth family to meet him at the Zebedee boatshop in Capernaum on Sunday, August 7, and Jesus crossed over with Andrew and Peter. But that very day a group of Pharisees called upon Mary to learn where Jesus was. Noting the nervousness of the family, they concluded that he was expected, installed themselves in her house, summoned reinforcements, and waited. Jude and Ruth tried several times to slip past them with a message, but it was of no avail. When David’s messengers told Jesus that the Pharisees were encamped on his mother’s doorstep, he made no attempt to go there. And so again, through no fault of either, Jesus and his earth family failed to meet.
ch35.b003: While the three tarried by the lake, a temple-tax collector drew Peter aside: “⟦Q 157:1.1⟧Does not your Master pay the temple tax?⟦/Q⟧” Peter sensed a trap and answered: “⟦Q 157:1.1⟧Why of course the Master pays the temple tax. You wait by the gate, and I will presently return with the tax.⟦/Q⟧” But Judas carried the funds, and Judas was across the lake. Jesus said: “⟦Q 157:1.2⟧If you have promised, then should you pay. But wherewith will you redeem your promise? Will you again become a fisherman that you may honor your word? Nevertheless, Peter, it is well in the circumstances that we pay the tax. Let us give these men no occasion for offense at our attitude.⟦/Q⟧” As Peter turned toward the boat, Jesus added, half-humorously: “⟦Q 157:1.4⟧Go hence! maybe you will catch the fish with the shekel in its mouth.⟦/Q⟧” A secret messenger of David had overheard everything; he and a fisherman friend presented Peter with several large baskets of fish, and the price of the catch, with what the messenger added, paid the tax for all three. In those days tales of treasure found in the mouths of fishes were commonplace, and so the episode later grew into the miracle recorded in Matthew’s Gospel. When it grew dark, the three slowly rowed away toward the eastern shore.
ch35.b005: On Monday, August 8, Jesus and the twelve were encamped in Magadan Park, near Bethsaida-Julias, when more than a hundred believers—evangelists, the women’s corps, and others devoted to the kingdom—came over from Capernaum for a conference. Many Pharisees came too, and by now some of the Sadducees had joined them in the effort to entrap Jesus. At the public meeting held before the closed conference, they heckled the Master and tried to disturb the assembly. Their leader called out: “⟦Q 157:2.1⟧Teacher, we would like you to give us a sign of your authority to teach, and then, when the same shall come to pass, all men will know that you have been sent by God.⟦/Q⟧”
ch35.b006: Jesus answered them: “⟦Q 157:2.1⟧When it is evening, you say it will be fair weather, for the heaven is red; in the morning it will be foul weather, for the heaven is red and lowering. When you see a cloud rising in the west, you say showers will come; when the wind blows from the south, you say scorching heat will come. How is it that you so well know how to discern the face of the heavens but are so utterly unable to discern the signs of the times? To those who would know the truth, already has a sign been given; but to an evil-minded and hypocritical generation no sign shall be given.⟦/Q⟧”
ch35.b007: At the evening conference it was decided that, when Jesus and the twelve returned from Caesarea-Philippi, they would undertake a united mission through all the cities and villages of the Decapolis. In dismissing the company the Master said: “⟦Q 157:2.2⟧I say to you, beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and the Sadducees.… It is not the fear of a dead religion that will save you but rather your faith in a living experience in the spiritual realities of the kingdom.… It is not the purpose of true religion merely to bring peace but rather to insure progress.⟦/Q⟧” He urged them not to stifle the feelings of service when they arose in the soul, and when love for a neighbor welled up in the heart, to give it expression “⟦Q 157:2.2⟧in intelligent ministry to the real needs of your fellows.⟦/Q⟧”
ch35.b009: Early Tuesday morning Jesus and the twelve set out for Caesarea-Philippi, the capital of the Tetrarch Philip’s domain. The town nestled in a valley of wondrous beauty between scenic hills, where the Jordan poured forth from an underground cave; the heights of Mount Hermon stood in full view to the north. Jesus had gone up Hermon early in his work for the kingdom, and now, entering upon its final epoch, he wished to return to that mount of trial and triumph, hoping the apostles might gain a new vision of their responsibilities and new strength for the trying times ahead. As they walked south of the Waters of Merom, the apostles fell to talking about their recent experiences in Phoenicia and elsewhere, how the message had been received, and how the different peoples regarded their Master.
ch35.b010: When they paused for lunch, seated under the mulberry trees, Jesus suddenly confronted them with the first question he had ever asked them concerning himself: “⟦Q 157:3.3⟧Who do men say that I am?⟦/Q⟧” He had spent long months teaching them the nature of the kingdom; now the time had come to teach them more about his own nature and his relation to it. More than half the apostles answered. They told him that all who knew him regarded him as a prophet or an extraordinary man; that even his enemies greatly feared him, explaining his powers by charging that he was in league with the prince of devils; that some in Judea and Samaria who had never met him believed he was John the Baptist risen from the dead. Peter added that at various times he had been compared with Moses, Elijah, Isaiah, and Jeremiah.
ch35.b011: When Jesus had heard them out, he rose to his feet. Looking down upon the twelve sitting about him in a semicircle, he pointed to them with a sweeping gesture of his hand and asked, with startling emphasis, “⟦Q 157:3.5⟧But who say you that I am?⟦/Q⟧” There was a moment of tense silence. The twelve never took their eyes off the Master. Then Simon Peter sprang to his feet and exclaimed: “⟦Q 157:3.5⟧You are the Deliverer, the Son of the living God.⟦/Q⟧” And the eleven who were sitting rose with one accord, showing that Peter had spoken for them all.
ch35.b012: Jesus beckoned them to be seated again and, still standing, said: “⟦Q 157:3.6⟧This has been revealed to you by my Father. The hour has come when you should know the truth about me. But for the time being I charge you that you tell this to no man. Let us go hence.⟦/Q⟧”
ch35.b014: They arrived late that evening at Caesarea-Philippi and stopped at the home of Celsus, who was expecting them. The apostles slept little that night; they sensed that a great event had taken place in their lives and in the work of the kingdom. Through most of the night and all that morning Simon Peter and Simon Zelotes labored earnestly with their brethren, urging them to accept the Master not merely as the Messiah but as the divine Son of the living God. Andrew remained the director of the apostolic corps, but Peter was becoming, by common consent, the spokesman of the twelve.
ch35.b015: At about noon on Wednesday, as they sat in Celsus’ garden, the Master appeared. They wore expressions of dignified solemnity, and all of them rose as he approached. Jesus relieved the tension with that friendly and fraternal smile so characteristic of him when his followers took themselves too seriously, and with a commanding gesture he motioned them to sit. Never again did the twelve rise to greet him; they saw that he did not approve of such outward show. After the meal, while they were discussing plans for the Decapolis tour, Jesus suddenly looked into their faces and asked whether, now that a full day had passed since they had assented to Peter’s declaration, they still held to their decision. The twelve stood, and Peter stepped a few paces forward: “⟦Q 157:4.4⟧Yes, Master, we do. We believe that you are the Son of the living God.⟦/Q⟧”
ch35.b016: Jesus, still standing, told them that they could not have reached this belief by mere human knowledge; it was a revelation of the spirit of his Father to their inmost souls. “⟦Q 157:4.5⟧Upon this rock of spiritual reality,⟦/Q⟧” he declared, “⟦Q 157:4.5⟧will I build the living temple of spiritual fellowship in the eternal realities of my Father’s kingdom. All the forces of evil and the hosts of sin shall not prevail against this human fraternity of the divine spirit.⟦/Q⟧” And while the Father’s spirit would ever be the guide of all who entered this fellowship, to them and their successors he delivered “⟦Q 157:4.5⟧the keys of the outward kingdom—the authority over things temporal—the social and economic features of this association of men and women as fellows of the kingdom.⟦/Q⟧” Again he charged them to tell no man, for the time being, that he was the Son of God.
ch35.b017: Jesus was beginning to have faith in the loyalty of his apostles. On this day the Master began to believe in the faith of his apostles, save one. And ever since, this same Jesus has been building that living temple upon the foundation of his divine sonship; those who become self-conscious sons of God are its human stones. When he had finished, he sent the twelve apart into the hills to seek wisdom, strength, and spiritual guidance until the evening meal.
ch35.b019: What was new in Peter’s confession was the clear recognition that Jesus was the Son of God, of his unquestioned divinity. The Jewish idea of a national deliverer had never included divinity; the Messiah was to be the “anointed one,” hardly “the Son of God.” In this second confession the emphasis fell on the combined nature, the supernal fact that he was both the Son of Man and the Son of God, and it was upon this union of the human with the divine that Jesus declared he would build the kingdom. For three years he had called himself the Son of Man while the apostles grew ever more insistent that he was the Jewish Messiah. He now gave up trying to convince them that he was not the Messiah, and resolved instead boldly to reveal what he is, and to leave their Messianic notions to themselves.
ch35.b020: Here Jesus entered upon the fourth and last stage of his life in the flesh, after childhood, youth, and the years of teaching and healing; it began at Caesarea-Philippi and would reach to the cross. Before Caesarea-Philippi he had presented the gospel as its master teacher; after it he appeared as the divine representative of the eternal Father, and he had to do all this as a human being, the Son of Man.
ch35.b021: They stayed another day with Celsus, waiting for funds, for the treasury was empty; that evening David Zebedee’s messengers arrived from Bethsaida with enough to carry the apostles until the Decapolis tour. That afternoon in the garden the apostles heard much that was new and strange. Jesus said: “⟦Q 157:6.9⟧The Son of Man came not to be ministered to, but to minister and to bestow his life as the gift for all. I declare to you that I have come to seek and to save those who are lost.⟦/Q⟧” He said: “Before Abraham was, I am.” He said: “⟦Q 157:6.12⟧My kingdom is not of this world.⟦/Q⟧” And he said: “⟦Q 157:6.13⟧Nevertheless, I tell you that the Father and I are one. He who has seen me has seen the Father.⟦/Q⟧” He told them, too, that he must presently leave this world and return to the work of his Father. The apostles listened in silence; they were stunned. They broke up into small groups to ponder his words. They had confessed that he was the Son of God, but they could not grasp the full meaning of what they had been led to do.
ch35.b023: That evening Andrew took it upon himself to talk personally and searchingly with each of his brethren, and with all but one the talks were heartening. Judas Iscariot had never opened himself freely to the head of the apostolic corps, and Andrew was now so troubled by his attitude that, late at night when the others were asleep, he went to Jesus. The Master said: “⟦Q 157:7.1⟧It is not amiss, Andrew, that you have come to me with this matter, but there is nothing more that we can do; only go on placing the utmost confidence in this apostle. And say nothing to his brethren concerning this talk with me.⟦/Q⟧” That was all Andrew could draw from him.
ch35.b024: Judas had been shocked by the death of John the Baptist, hurt by the Master’s rebukes, disappointed when Jesus refused to be made king, humiliated when he fled from the Pharisees, and lately depressed by an empty treasury; he missed the stimulus of the multitudes, and he took the warning about the leaven of the Pharisees as a veiled reference to himself. The others passed through the same trials, but they loved Jesus, and they went with him to the bitter end. The great mistake of Judas was this: time and again, when Jesus sent the apostles off to pray, Judas, instead of seeking sincere communion with the spiritual forces of the universe, indulged in thoughts of human fear, nursed subtle doubts about Jesus’ mission, and gave way to his unfortunate tendency to harbor feelings of revenge.
ch35.b025: On the morning of Friday, August 12, Jesus said to the twelve: “⟦Q 157:7.5⟧Lay in provisions and prepare yourselves for a journey to yonder mountain, where the spirit bids me go to be endowed for the finish of my work on earth. And I would take my brethren along that they may also be strengthened for the trying times of going with me through this experience.⟦/Q⟧”
ch36.title: The Mount of Transfiguration
ch36.b001: The Foot of Mount Hermon, August A.D. 29
ch36.b002: It was near sundown on Friday, August 12, A.D. 29, when Jesus and the twelve reached the foot of Mount Hermon, close to the very place where the lad Tiglath had once waited while the Master went up alone to settle the spiritual destinies of Urantia and technically to end the Lucifer rebellion. Here they stayed two days in spiritual preparation. Jesus wished that all his apostles might share what was to come, but they could not attain the needed spiritual levels, so he took only the three who usually accompanied him on such vigils—Peter, James, and John. It was not that they were better prepared or more fit than the others. None of the twelve was spiritually qualified for this experience.
ch36.b003: Early on Monday morning, August 15, six days after Peter’s confession under the mulberry trees, Jesus and the three began the ascent. Shortly before noon they reached a place about halfway up, and over lunch Jesus told them something of his days in the hills east of the Jordan after his baptism and of his former visit to this lonely retreat. About three o’clock on that beautiful afternoon he took leave of them: “⟦Q 158:1.6⟧I go apart by myself for a season to commune with the Father and his messengers; I bid you tarry here.⟦/Q⟧” He withdrew for a long conference with Gabriel and the Father Melchizedek and did not return until about six. Seeing their anxiety, he said: “⟦Q 158:1.6⟧Why were you afraid? You well know I must be about my Father’s business; wherefore do you doubt when I am not with you? I now declare that the Son of Man has chosen to go through his full life in your midst and as one of you. Be of good cheer; I will not leave you until my work is finished.⟦/Q⟧”
ch36.b005: Over their meager evening meal Peter asked, “⟦Q 158:1.7⟧How long do we remain on this mountain away from our brethren?⟦/Q⟧” Jesus answered: “⟦Q 158:1.7⟧Until you shall see the glory of the Son of Man and know that whatsoever I have declared to you is true.⟦/Q⟧” They sat about the glowing embers of their fire talking over the affairs of the Lucifer rebellion until darkness drew on and the apostles’ eyes grew heavy, for they had started very early that morning.
ch36.b006: When they had been asleep about half an hour, a crackling sound near by suddenly woke them. To their amazement and consternation they saw Jesus in intimate converse with two brilliant beings clothed in the light of the celestial world, and Jesus’ face and form shone with the luminosity of a heavenly light. The three spoke in a strange language. From certain things said, Peter conjectured that the beings were Moses and Elijah; in reality they were Gabriel and the Father Melchizedek. At Jesus’ request the physical controllers had arranged for the apostles to witness the scene.
ch36.b007: The apostles were so frightened that they were slow to collect their wits. Peter recovered first, and as the dazzling vision faded and they saw Jesus standing alone, he said: “⟦Q 158:1.9⟧Jesus, Master, it is good to have been here. We rejoice to see this glory. We are loath to go back down to the inglorious world. If you are willing, let us abide here, and we will erect three tents, one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.⟦/Q⟧” He said it out of sheer confusion.
ch36.b008: While Peter was still speaking, a silvery cloud drew near and overshadowed the four of them. The apostles fell on their faces in fear, and they heard a voice, the same that had spoken at Jesus’ baptism: “⟦Q 158:1.10⟧This is my beloved Son; give heed to him.⟦/Q⟧” When the cloud vanished, Jesus was alone with them. He reached down and touched them, saying: “⟦Q 158:1.10⟧Arise and be not afraid; you shall see greater things than this.⟦/Q⟧” But they were truly afraid, and they were a silent and thoughtful trio as they made ready, shortly before midnight, to descend.
ch36.b009: What the three had seen was only a fleeting glimpse of a celestial pageant. Gabriel brought Jesus assurance that the Eternal Son accepted the fullness of his bestowal, and the Infinite Spirit testified through the Father Melchizedek. But the Father did not indicate that the bestowal was finished; his unseen presence only bore witness through Jesus’ Personalized Adjuster. The Master could have relinquished the struggle that day and returned to the rule of his universe; instead he chose to pursue the mortal bestowal to its natural end, and three of his apostles watched in amazement as the celestial messengers departed and left him alone to finish his earth life as the Son of Man and the Son of God.
ch36.b011: For about half the way down not a word was spoken. Then Jesus said: “⟦Q 158:2.1⟧Make certain that you tell no man, not even your brethren, what you have seen and heard on this mountain until the Son of Man has risen from the dead.⟦/Q⟧” The three were shocked: he had just been transfigured in glory, and now he spoke of “rising from the dead”! Peter shuddered at the thought and seized on the first diversion that came to mind: “⟦Q 158:2.2⟧Master, why is it that the scribes say that Elijah must first come before the Messiah shall appear?⟦/Q⟧”
ch36.b012: Jesus, knowing that Peter wanted to avoid all talk of death and resurrection, answered: “⟦Q 158:2.2⟧Elijah indeed comes first to prepare the way for the Son of Man, who must suffer many things and finally be rejected. But I tell you that Elijah has already come, and they received him not but did to him whatsoever they willed.⟦/Q⟧” The three perceived that he meant John the Baptist. As they went on down, he said to them: “⟦Q 158:2.4⟧… If you thus choose to follow the inclination of your own wills, you must prepare to suffer many disappointments and experience many trials, but the training which I have given you should suffice to bring you triumphantly through even these sorrows of your own choosing.⟦/Q⟧”
ch36.b013: The Boy They Could Not Heal
ch36.b014: Shortly before breakfast on Tuesday they reached the camp and found a crowd of about fifty people—the nine apostles and an equal mixture of Jerusalem scribes and believing disciples who had tracked them from Magadan—engaged in loud dispute. The chief controversy concerned James of Safed, a citizen of Tiberias and a minor official of Herod Antipas, who had arrived the day before. His only son, about fourteen years old, was severely afflicted with epilepsy and was also possessed by one of the wandering, rebellious midwayers then uncontrolled on earth. For almost two weeks the father had searched for Jesus along the western borders of Philip’s domains.
ch36.b015: When he came upon the nine at noon, most of them had fallen into their old temptation of arguing who should be greatest in the coming kingdom. Then Simon Zelotes and Judas Iscariot stepped forward: “⟦Q 158:4.6⟧We can heal him; you need not wait for the Master’s return. We are ambassadors of the kingdom; no longer do we hold these things in secret. Jesus is the Deliverer, and the keys of the kingdom have been delivered to us.⟦/Q⟧” Simon laid his hand on the boy’s head, looked into his eyes, and commanded: “⟦Q 158:4.6⟧Come out of him, you unclean spirit; in the name of Jesus obey me.⟦/Q⟧” But the lad only had a more violent fit, and the scribes mocked. After a season of prayer Andrew tried again and also failed. He confessed defeat and asked the father to stay: “⟦Q 158:4.7⟧Perhaps this sort goes not out except by the Master’s personal command.⟦/Q⟧” So while the three came down the mountain in exultation, the nine lay sleepless in their confusion and humiliation.
ch36.b016: As Jesus drew near, the nine were more than relieved. Before they could answer his question about their dispute, the father knelt at his feet: his only child foamed at the mouth, fell like one dead, and had often been cast into water and fire; “⟦Q 158:5.1⟧His life is worse than death.⟦/Q⟧” The apostles had tried and failed. “⟦Q 158:5.1⟧And now, Master, will you do this for us, will you heal my son?⟦/Q⟧”
ch36.b017: Jesus touched the father and bade him rise, and gave the apostles a searching look. Then he said to all who stood there: “⟦Q 158:5.2⟧O faithless and perverse generation, how long shall I bear with you? How long shall I be with you? How long ere you learn that the works of faith come not forth at the bidding of doubting unbelief?⟦/Q⟧” He said, “Bring hither your son.” As they talked, the boy was seized with a violent attack and lay before them as one dead. The father knelt again: “⟦Q 158:5.2⟧If you can cure him, I beseech you to have compassion on us and deliver us from this affliction.⟦/Q⟧” Jesus looked down into his anxious face: “⟦Q 158:5.2⟧Question not my Father’s power of love, only the sincerity and reach of your faith. All things are possible to him who really believes.⟦/Q⟧” And James of Safed spoke those long-remembered words of mingled faith and doubt: “⟦Q 158:5.2⟧Lord, I believe. I pray you help my unbelief.⟦/Q⟧”
ch36.b018: Jesus took the lad by the hand: “⟦Q 158:5.3⟧I will do this in accordance with my Father’s will and in honor of living faith. My son, arise! Come out of him, disobedient spirit, and go not back into him.⟦/Q⟧” Placing the boy’s hand in the father’s, he said: “⟦Q 158:5.3⟧Go your way. The Father has granted the desire of your soul.⟦/Q⟧” Everyone present, even Jesus’ enemies, was astonished, and the lad was cured from that hour. For the three just come from the ecstasy of the mountain, it was a hard return.
ch36.b020: That night, after they had eaten and rested in Celsus’ garden at Caesarea-Philippi, Thomas asked the Master to instruct them concerning their defeat. Jesus told them that while he went up the mountain to seek his Father’s will, they who were left to pray had yielded to their old tendency to seek preferred places in a material kingdom, though he had told them again and again that his kingdom is not of this world. “Spiritual greatness,” he said, “⟦Q 158:6.3⟧consists in an understanding love that is Godlike and not in an enjoyment of the exercise of material power for the exaltation of self. In what you attempted, in which you so completely failed, your purpose was not pure. Your motive was not divine. Your ideal was not spiritual. Your ambition was not altruistic.⟦/Q⟧” And he asked: “⟦Q 158:6.4⟧Must you always have material manifestations as an attraction for the spiritual realities of the kingdom?⟦/Q⟧” Then he declared to all what he had told the three on the mountain: “⟦Q 158:6.5⟧The Son of Man now enters upon the last phase of the bestowal.… And remember what I am saying to you: The Son of Man will be put to death, but he shall rise again.⟦/Q⟧” They went to bed sorrowful and bewildered. Only after his resurrection did they recall it all.
ch36.b022: Early on Wednesday, to elude the scribes and the crowd, Jesus led them south by the Damascus road through Galilee. As they rested in the shade after lunch, Andrew asked whether the Master was speaking in parables. Jesus answered that because they had confessed him as the Son of God he must now tell them plainly: the Son of Man must go to Jerusalem, suffer many things, be rejected by the scribes, the elders, and the chief priests, be killed, and be raised from the dead. “⟦Q 158:7.3⟧And I speak not a parable to you; I speak the truth to you that you may be prepared for these events when they suddenly come upon us.⟦/Q⟧” Simon Peter rushed to him, laid a hand on his shoulder, and said: “⟦Q 158:7.3⟧Master, be it far from us to contend with you, but I declare that these things shall never happen to you.⟦/Q⟧”
ch36.b023: Peter spoke out of love. But the Master’s human nature recognized in those affectionate words a subtle temptation to turn aside from doing his Father’s will to the end, and he turned upon Peter and the others: “⟦Q 158:7.4⟧Get you behind me. You savor of the spirit of the adversary, the tempter. When you talk in this manner, you are not on my side but rather on the side of our enemy. In this way do you make your love for me a stumbling block to my doing the Father’s will. Mind not the ways of men but rather the will of God.⟦/Q⟧” When they had recovered from the shock, he went on: “⟦Q 158:7.5⟧If any man would come after me, let him disregard himself, take up his responsibilities daily, and follow me. For whosoever would save his life selfishly, shall lose it, but whosoever loses his life for my sake and the gospel’s, shall save it. What does it profit a man to gain the whole world and lose his own soul?⟦/Q⟧”
ch36.b024: Only a few times did the apostles see that flashing eye and hear such swift rebuke; Jesus was patient with their failings, but not with a threat to his doing of the Father’s will. They were stunned. Yet not one of them was minded to forsake him. He was not sending them alone into the conflict; he was leading them, and he asked only that they bravely follow.
ch36.b025: At twilight, at Peter’s house in Capernaum, Jesus asked what they had been discussing so earnestly on the road. They held their peace; many had resumed the old argument over who should be greatest. Jesus beckoned to one of Peter’s little ones and set the child among them: “⟦Q 158:8.1⟧Verily, verily, I say to you, except you turn about and become more like this child, you will make little progress in the kingdom of heaven. Whosoever shall humble himself and become as this little one, the same shall become greatest in the kingdom of heaven. And whoso receives such a little one receives me.⟦/Q⟧” Whoever caused one of these little ones to stumble, he said, it would be better for him to be cast into the sea with a millstone about his neck. “⟦Q 158:8.1⟧But most of all, see that you despise not one of these little ones, for their angels do always behold the faces of the heavenly hosts.⟦/Q⟧” Then they entered the boat and sailed across to Magadan.
ch37.title: The Decapolis and Rodan
ch37.b002: When Jesus and the twelve returned to Magadan Park, almost a hundred evangelists and disciples, the women’s corps among them, were waiting, ready to begin the tour of the Decapolis at once. On Thursday morning, August 18, the Master called them together and directed that each apostle should pair himself with one of the twelve evangelists, and that with the other evangelists they should go out in twelve groups to the cities and villages of the region. The women’s corps and the rest of the disciples were to stay with him. He allotted four weeks to the tour and told them to be back at Magadan not later than Friday, September 16, promising to visit them often in the meantime. Through that month the twelve groups labored in Gerasa, Gamala, Hippos, Zaphon, Gadara, Abila, Edrei, Philadelphia, Heshbon, Dium, Scythopolis, and many other cities. Throughout the tour no miracles of healing or other extraordinary events occurred. It was a month of teaching and of quiet fellowship.
ch37.b004: One evening at Hippos, where Simon Peter was in charge, a disciple asked about forgiveness, and Jesus answered with the shepherd who leaves the ninety and nine to search for the one that has gone astray, keeps up his quest until he finds it, lays it on his shoulder, and goes home rejoicing, calling to his neighbors, “⟦Q 159:1.2⟧Rejoice with me, for I have found my sheep that was lost.⟦/Q⟧” Then he said: “In your religion God may receive repentant sinners; in the gospel of the kingdom the Father goes forth to find them even before they have seriously thought of repentance.
ch37.b005: “⟦Q 159:1.3⟧The Father in heaven loves his children, and therefore should you learn to love one another; the Father in heaven forgives you your sins; therefore should you learn to forgive one another.⟦/Q⟧” If a brother sinned against them, they were to go to him alone and with tact and patience show him his fault; if he would not listen, to go again with one or two mutual friends; and if he still refused, to tell the whole story to the congregation and let the brotherhood act as it deemed wise. They could not sit in judgment on the souls of their fellows or forgive sins, he said, but it had been committed to their hands to maintain temporal order in the kingdom on earth. “⟦Q 159:1.3⟧And all this is ever true, for, where two or three believers are gathered together, there am I in the midst of them.⟦/Q⟧”
ch37.b006: Peter asked: “⟦Q 159:1.4⟧Lord, how often shall my brother sin against me, and I forgive him? Until seven times?⟦/Q⟧” Jesus answered: “⟦Q 159:1.4⟧Not only seven times but even to seventy times and seven.⟦/Q⟧” And he told of a king who called his stewards to account. One chief retainer owed him ten thousand talents and could not pay; the king ordered his property seized and his children sold, but when the man fell on his face and begged for time, the king was moved with compassion and forgave the whole debt. That same steward then went out, found a subordinate who owed him a mere hundred denarii, took him by the throat, and had him cast into prison. When the king heard of it, he called the man back: “⟦Q 159:1.5⟧You are a wicked and unworthy steward. When you sought for compassion, I freely forgave you your entire debt. Why did you not also show mercy to your fellow steward, even as I showed mercy to you?⟦/Q⟧” And he delivered him to the jailers. “⟦Q 159:1.5⟧I say to all of you,⟦/Q⟧” Jesus concluded, “⟦Q 159:1.5⟧Freely you have received the good things of the kingdom; therefore freely give to your fellows on earth.⟦/Q⟧” So he taught the danger and unfairness of sitting in personal judgment upon one’s fellows. Discipline must be maintained, but by the wisdom of the brotherhood, for the verdict of an individual is easily warped by prejudice or passion.
ch37.b008: At Gamala, after the evening’s questions and answers, John said: “⟦Q 159:2.1⟧Master, yesterday I went over to Ashtaroth to see a man who was teaching in your name and even claiming to be able to cast out devils. Now this fellow had never been with us, neither does he follow after us; therefore I forbade him to do such things.⟦/Q⟧” Jesus said: “⟦Q 159:2.1⟧Forbid him not. Do you not perceive that this gospel of the kingdom shall presently be proclaimed in all the world? How can you expect that all who will believe the gospel shall be subject to your direction? Rejoice that already our teaching has begun to manifest itself beyond the bounds of our personal influence.… My son, in matters of this sort it would be better for you to reckon that he who is not against us is for us.⟦/Q⟧” Many in generations to come, he said, would do strange things in his name, and he would not forbid them. “⟦Q 159:2.1⟧I tell you that, even when a cup of cold water is given to a thirsty soul, the Father’s messengers shall ever make record of such a service of love.⟦/Q⟧”
ch37.b009: John was greatly perplexed. Had he not heard the Master say, “⟦Q 159:2.2⟧He who is not with me is against me⟦/Q⟧”? He did not yet see that the one saying concerned a man’s personal relation to the spiritual teachings of the kingdom, and the other the outward relations between groups of believers in the coming world-wide brotherhood. Yet he often recounted this lesson in his later labors. As for the man, Aden, he paid no heed to John’s injunction; he raised up a considerable company of believers at Kanata before going on into Mesopotamia. He had come to believe through the testimony of the demented man whom Jesus had healed near Kheresa.
ch37.b011: At Edrei, where Thomas and his associates worked, Jesus spent a day and a night, and in the evening’s discussion he set forth the principles that should guide all who teach the gospel. Always respect the personality of man, he told them. Never should a righteous cause be promoted by force; spiritual victories can be won only by spiritual power. Do not crush a man’s mind with the mere weight of logic or overawe it with shrewd eloquence; do not appeal to fear, pity, or mere sentiment, but directly to the divine spirit that dwells within the minds of men. “⟦Q 159:3.2⟧Remember that I have said: ‘Behold, I stand at the door and knock, and if any man will open, I will come in.’⟦/Q⟧”
ch37.b012: It was the purpose of the gospel, he said, to restore self-respect to those who had lost it and to restrain it in those who had too much. They must not only condemn the wrongs in their pupils’ lives but generously recognize what was praiseworthy; they must not indulge in sarcasm at the expense of simple-minded brethren or be cynical with the fear-ridden; they must never try to frighten men into the kingdom. Strong feelings of emotion are not the same as the leadings of the divine spirit. All who pass from the life of the flesh to the life of the spirit must cross a fringe of conflict, “⟦Q 159:3.7⟧but remember: The gospel yoke is easy and the burden of truth is light.⟦/Q⟧” Men die searching for the very God who lives within them. “⟦Q 159:3.8⟧Faith is to religion what sails are to a ship; it is an addition of power, not an added burden of life.⟦/Q⟧”
ch37.b013: And he said: “⟦Q 159:3.10⟧You shall not portray your teacher as a man of sorrows. Future generations shall know also the radiance of our joy, the buoyance of our good will, and the inspiration of our good humor.⟦/Q⟧” Believers should not lean on the insecure props of false sympathy or indulge in self-pity. Entering the kingdom does not make one immune to the accidents of time or the catastrophes of nature; believing the gospel will not keep a man out of trouble, but it will make him unafraid when trouble comes. “⟦Q 159:3.13⟧I do not promise to deliver you from the waters of adversity, but I do promise to go with you through all of them.⟦/Q⟧” Those who heard these sayings treasured them in their hearts and often recited them for the brethren who had not been present.
ch37.b015: At Abila, where Nathaniel labored, the apostle drew the Master aside after the evening session. Some of Jesus’ words seemed to detract from the authority of the Hebrew scriptures, and Nathaniel asked: “⟦Q 159:4.1⟧Master, could you trust me to know the truth about the Scriptures? I observe that you teach us only a portion of the sacred writings—the best as I view it—and I infer that you reject the teachings of the rabbis to the effect that the words of the law are the very words of God, having been with God in heaven even before the times of Abraham and Moses. What is the truth about the Scriptures?⟦/Q⟧”
ch37.b016: Jesus agreed to tell him, on condition that he not repeat it to his brethren, who were not all ready to receive it. The Scriptures, he said, had been gathered together only in recent times. “⟦Q 159:4.3⟧These writings are the work of men, some of them holy men, others not so holy. The teachings of these books represent the views and extent of enlightenment of the times in which they had their origin.⟦/Q⟧” If Jonah had never lived, the truth of that story, the love of God for Nineveh and the so-called heathen, would be no less precious. But the writings also contain much that misrepresents the Father. “⟦Q 159:4.5⟧Nathaniel, never permit yourself for one moment to believe the Scripture records which tell you that the God of love directed your forefathers to go forth in battle to slay all their enemies—men, women, and children. Such records are the words of men, not very holy men, and they are not the word of God.⟦/Q⟧”
ch37.b017: Still, he said, faulty and human as they were, the Scriptures “⟦Q 159:4.3⟧do constitute the best collection of religious wisdom and spiritual truth to be found in all the world at this time.⟦/Q⟧” The most deplorable thing was not the error of their supposed perfection but their misinterpretation by tradition-bound scribes, and the use of both to resist the gospel. He was making no written record of his own teachings, lest after his departure his followers divide into sundry groups of contenders over its interpretation. “⟦Q 159:4.8⟧Mark you well my words, Nathaniel, nothing which human nature has touched can be regarded as infallible.… The creature may crave infallibility, but only the Creators possess it.⟦/Q⟧” Nathaniel was enlightened, and shocked. He pondered this talk long in the depths of his soul but told no one of it until after Jesus’ ascension.
ch37.b019: At Philadelphia, where James was working, Jesus spoke of the positive nature of the gospel. When he urged his hearers to feed their souls on the best of the Scriptures, James asked how to choose the better passages. Jesus answered: “Yes, James, when you read the Scriptures look for those eternally true and divinely beautiful teachings, such as:

ch37.b020.en: “Create in me a clean heart, O Lord.

ch37.b021.en: “The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want.

ch37.b022.en: “You should love your neighbor as yourself.

ch37.b023.en: “For I, the Lord your God, will hold your right hand, saying, fear not; I will help you.

ch37.b024.en: “Neither shall the nations learn war any more.”

ch37.b025: So, day by day, he took the cream of the Hebrew scriptures into the gospel, and he put the spirit of positive action into the passive doctrines of the old religion. He opposed even purely passive nonresistance. “⟦Q 159:5.9⟧When an enemy smites you on one cheek,⟦/Q⟧” he said, “⟦Q 159:5.9⟧do not stand there dumb and passive but in positive attitude turn the other; that is, do the best thing possible actively to lead your brother in error away from the evil paths into the better ways of righteous living.⟦/Q⟧” He taught them three ways of meeting evil: to return evil for evil, the positive but unrighteous way; to suffer evil without complaint or resistance, the purely negative way; and to return good for evil, asserting the will so as to master the situation and overcome evil with good, the positive and righteous way.
ch37.b026: One of the apostles once asked: “⟦Q 159:5.15⟧Master, what should I do if a stranger forced me to carry his pack for a mile?⟦/Q⟧” Jesus answered: “⟦Q 159:5.15⟧Do not sit down and sigh for relief while you berate the stranger under your breath. Righteousness comes not from such passive attitudes. If you can think of nothing more effectively positive to do, you can at least carry the pack a second mile. That will of a certainty challenge the unrighteous and ungodly stranger.⟦/Q⟧” The Jews had heard of a God who would forgive repentant sinners; not until Jesus came did men hear of a God who goes in search of the lost sheep and rejoices to find them.
ch37.b027: On Friday, September 16, the whole corps of workers assembled at Magadan Park. The mission had been moderately successful: hundreds of souls had entered the kingdom, and the apostles and evangelists had learned to work without the immediate presence of their Master. David’s messengers came with reports from believers throughout Palestine; they had also served through these dark days as collectors of funds for Jesus and for the families of the apostles and evangelists. The week that followed was the last rest Jesus and his associates would know.
ch37.b029: On Sunday, September 18, most of the apostles went home to their families, and Jesus enjoyed almost complete rest. But Nathaniel and Thomas were kept busy by a Greek philosopher from Alexandria named Rodan, who had lately become a disciple through the work of one of Abner’s associates there. He had come to Magadan to harmonize his philosophy with Jesus’ teaching and to hear the gospel firsthand. The Master received him graciously but declined to enter into discussion himself; instead he told Nathaniel and Thomas to listen to all Rodan had to say and to tell him about the gospel in return.
ch37.b030: Beginning early Monday, Rodan gave ten addresses to the two apostles and some two dozen believers who chanced to be at Magadan. Human life, he said, consists of urges, desires, and lures, and strong character comes from raising them into the social art of living and the pursuit of higher ideals. The more complex civilization becomes, the harder the art of living. The first step in solving any problem is frankly to recognize it, and “⟦Q 160:1.7⟧only a brave person is willing honestly to admit, and fearlessly to face, what a sincere and logical mind discovers.⟦/Q⟧” Friendship and marriage he praised as the noblest school of character, and he pointed out that “⟦Q 160:2.7⟧the Master never sends you out alone to labor for the extension of the kingdom; he always sends you out two and two.⟦/Q⟧” He warned that life becomes a burden unless one learns to fail gracefully, for “⟦Q 160:4.14⟧wisdom comes only from the experiences of adjustment to the results of one’s failures.⟦/Q⟧”
ch37.b031: Above all he was moved by Jesus’ habit of going apart to commune with the Father. “⟦Q 160:3.1⟧Emotional excitement is not the ideal spiritual stimulus,⟦/Q⟧” he said. “⟦Q 160:3.1⟧Excitement does not augment energy; it rather exhausts the powers of both mind and body. Whence then comes the energy to do these great things? Look to your Master. Even now he is out in the hills taking in power while we are here giving out energy.⟦/Q⟧” Meditation makes the contact of mind with spirit, relaxation determines the capacity for receiving it, “⟦Q 160:3.1⟧and this interchange of strength for weakness, courage for fear, the will of God for the mind of self, constitutes worship.⟦/Q⟧” At the close of his addresses Rodan confessed: “⟦Q 160:5.8⟧My brethren, I am a believer, I have embarked; I am on my way with you in this eternal venture.⟦/Q⟧”
ch37.b033: On Sunday evening, September 25, Jesus surprised everyone by announcing that early the next morning he and the twelve would leave for Jerusalem to attend the feast of tabernacles. Nathaniel and Thomas, still deep in debate with Rodan, obtained leave to stay a few days longer. One point remained unsettled: the personality of God. Rodan accepted all they taught about God’s attributes but contended that the Father cannot be a person as man conceives it, since personality requires full communication between equals, and God has no equal. The two apostles had asked Jesus to come to their rescue, but he would only say to Thomas: “⟦Q 161:1.3⟧It matters little what idea of the Father you may entertain as long as you are spiritually acquainted with the ideal of his infinite and eternal nature.⟦/Q⟧”
ch37.b034: By Monday night Thomas gave up. But by Tuesday night Nathaniel had won Rodan over, step by step. The Father, he reasoned, does enjoy equal communication with the Eternal Son and the Infinite Spirit. Jesus, who is one with the Father, communicates perfectly with men as well, so that his personality demonstrates the personality of God. And God must be a personality, since he is the Creator and the destiny of all personality. Rodan said: “⟦Q 161:1.11⟧I am convinced.… I am now convinced that, while God must be infinitely more than a personality, he cannot be anything less. I am satisfied to end the argument and to accept Jesus as the personal revelation of the Father.⟦/Q⟧”
ch37.b035: Then Nathaniel and Thomas told Rodan why they believed in the Master’s divinity. He was the most truly unselfish person they had ever known, the friend even of sinners, who dared to love his enemies. He did not hesitate to reprove them, but it was plain that he loved them. He prayed for them and with them but never asked them to pray for him. He prayed like a man but performed like a God, and said the most tremendous things—“Before Abraham was, I am”—with childlike naturalness. “⟦Q 161:2.10⟧We know he is human, we are sure of that, but we are almost equally sure that he is also divine. We believe that he is divine. We are convinced that he is the Son of Man and the Son of God.⟦/Q⟧”
ch37.b036: When the talks were ended, Nathaniel and Thomas hurried to Jerusalem and joined their fellow apostles on Friday of that week, and the others learned much from their account. Rodan went back to Alexandria and long taught his philosophy in the school of Meganta. He became a mighty man in the later affairs of the kingdom, and remained a faithful believer to the end, yielding up his life in Greece with others when the persecutions were at their height.
